summary.text: 笠岡ラーメン（かさおかラーメン）は、岡山県笠岡市のご当地ラーメン。「鶏そば」や「鶏ラーメン」、「かしわラーメン」などとも呼ばれる。
summary.license: CC BY-SA 4.0

summary.text: Okayama Prefecture's catch of octopuses is among the largest in the country. The sea near Shimotsui, Kurashiki has a particularly swift tidal current even for the Seto Inland Sea. They say that the octopuses that grow there have a characteristic chewiness, and their meat is firm and delicious. Kurashiki's special product is "takomeshi (octopus with rice)." For this dish, the octopus is cut into chunks and cooked with rice, and the quality of the ingredients, whose smell of the sea spreads out in abundance, is outstanding.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

name.kana: てのべそうめんのばちじる
name.en: Tenobe Somen no Bach-ijiru (Hand-pulled Somen Bachi Soup)

summary.text: "The Kamogata-cho area of Asakuchi City", located in the southwestern part of Okayama Prefecture, has flourished as a production center of "hand-pulled noodles" since the Edo period (1603-1868) due to its sunny climate and availability of high-quality water, salt, and wheat. The ends of the "hand-pulled somen noodles" that are attached to utensils during the production process are called bachi, so named because they resemble a "Japanese shamisen bachi (plectrum)".
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

name.ja: あみとだいこんの煮付け
name.kana: あみとだいこんのにつけ
name.zh_tw: あみとだいこんの煮付け
name.en: Ami to Daikon no Nitsuke (Boiled Mysids and Daikon Radish)

summary.text: "Ami to Daikon no Nitsuke (Boiled Mysids and Daikon Radish)" is a dish made by simmering mysids, daikon radish, and ginger in sugar, sake, and soy sauce, boasting a traditional taste that heralds the fall season in the Seto Inland Sea. It is thought that this dish was invented to enjoy mysids together with daikon radish, which are available around the exact same time of year. Mysids have a good amount of fat, so when cooked with daikon radish, they are a deliciously perfect match.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

name.en: Buri Zouni (Japanese Amberjack Soup with Mochi Rice Cakes)

summary.text: Soup with mochi rice cakes is an indispensable dish during the New Year. Various forms of the soup exist depending on the region. In Okayama Prefecture's southern area, near the sea, the standard is to put Japanese amberjack in the soup. The Japanese amberjack is a fish that is called by the different names "yazuinada," "hamachi," and "buri (amberjack)" as it grows larger. Thus, the fish is considered a good omen and is used for auspicious seated receptions.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

summary.text: Takakibi came from mainland China and is a type of corn. Also known as "sorghum millet," it is different from the type of "corn" native to the United States. As the name "takakibi" implies, it grows up to 3 meters tall and produces ears with many small reddish-brown kernels at the tip. Perhaps due to the difference in climate, the takkibi is sticky and has a savory flavor unlike its Chinese counterpart. When dumplings are made from takakibi flour, they are smooth, mild, and delicious on the tongue.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

summary.text: Niimi City has a soil unsuitable for rice cultivation, and buckwheat has long been cultivated in the area. Kenchin-soba, which makes use of this buckwheat, is a hot soba noodle topped with kenchin soup, which is made by simmering vegetables such as tofu, radish, carrots, and gobou(=burdock) root in a soy sauce-based chicken broth.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

name.ja: いしもちじゃこの唐揚げ
name.kana: いしもちじゃこのからあげ
name.zh_tw: いしもちじゃこの唐揚げ

summary.text: Ishimochi Jako is a small fish caught in the Seto Inland Sea from spring to summer. In some areas, it is called nebuto, and its standard Japanese name is tenjikudai. Because the otolith, a stone-like bone in the head, is larger than those of other fish, it cannot be eaten whole, but rather its head must be removed before cooking. Because it is a small fish, it has little flesh, but when fried and eaten bone by bone, it has a subtle sweetness to it. It is sweet and sticky, and is sometimes eaten as dumplings.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

summary.text: The Mimasaka area is a nature-rich area located in the northern part of Okayama Prefecture. It is known for its abundant population of wild boars and deer, contributing to a long-standing local tradition of consuming wild boar and deer meat. Particularly, wild boar dishes are famous as a winter specialty in the Mimasaka area. "Shisshi Nabe(=Wild boar hot pot) ", known as "shishi-nabe," is enjoyed by many, including local hunters and families, making it a beloved and popular dish in the region.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

summary.text: "Iidako(= Ocellated octopus)" are often caught in Okayama Prefecture in the Shimotsui area in the Kojima region of Kurashiki City in southern Japan. It is named "iidako" (meaning "rice octopus") because it carries many rice-grain-shaped eggs inside its body.The eggs are about 5-6 mm in diameter and each octopus contains about 200-500 eggs. Add salt, fir thoroughly, and drain before boiling. "Iidako" have ink, but even though squid ink is frowned upon, "the ink is worth the price of an iidako".
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

summary.text: "Tsuyama Horumon Udon" is a dish where fresh mixed horumon (beef or pork offal) is generously mixed and grilled together with udon (thick wheat noodles), coated with a miso or soy sauce-based sauce. The Tsuyama region, located in the northern part of Okayama Prefecture, has been a historical hub for the distribution of cattle and horses. Dating back to the year 705 AD, records indicate that a cattle and horse market was held in Tsuyama.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

summary.text: Matsuri-zushi, also called "Okayama-bara-zushi" or "Bizen-bara-zushi," is made for festivals, celebrations, and entertaining guests in the Bizen-Okayama area. It is a gorgeous chirashizushi filled with vegetables, seafood, and rich ingredients from the Seto Inland Sea. During the Edo period (1603-1867), Lord Mitsumasa Ikeda, the feudal lord of Okayama, issued a decree to economize, telling the common people to eat only one soup and one vegetable so that they would not be extravagant.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

name.en: Demi Katsu Don (Demi-glace Sauced Pork Cutlet on Rice)

summary.text: Okayama Demikatsu Don,” a local bowl in Okayama, features freshly fried pork cutlet topped with piping hot demi-glace sauce. It is said to have been created by the founder of the longstanding Okayama restaurant “Ajitsukasa Nomura.” Impressed by the taste of demi-glace sauce in Tokyo hotels, the founder wondered if it could be utilized in his own restaurant. In Okayama, some regions also refer to green peas as "Alaska," and these "Alaska" peas add a colorful touch, evoking a nostalgic Western-style dish.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

name.en: Kinira-no-Ohitashi (Boiled Yellow Chives in Ponzu Soy Sauce)

summary.text: Ki Nira is a specialty of Okayama Prefecture which accounts for 70% of the national production. It is said to have been cultivated circa 1872 in the Musa and Tamagashi areas of Okayama City. Through a unique cultivation method called "light shielding cultivation," which sunlight is blocked, it takes on a vibrant pastel yellow color. In addition to the inherent sweetness of chives, its fibers are soft enough to be enjoyed raw. Originally, it was discovered during the process of covering chives to soften them for cultivation.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

summary.text: Perilla seeds are plucked from the stems and added to soy sauce for flavoring when eating sashimi, as well as being boiled in tsukudani (food boiled in soy sauce) and pickled in salt. In the areas around Mimasaka, they are often boiled in tsukudani and served as an accompaniment for rice. The combination of the taste of perilla seeds with soy sauce and mirin(=sweet rice wine) creates a spicy and delicious flavor.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

summary.text: The history of funameshi goes along with the history of Kojima Bay reclamation. The southern area of Okayama Prefecture has long been developed with rice paddies formed by reclamation. Full-scale development of new rice paddies began in the Edo period (1603-1867), and our predecessors labored hard to cultivate the land. Blessed with a water environment that connects rice paddies, canals, rivers, and Lake Kojima, the area is home to reeds, crucian carp, and freshwater mussel.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

name.kana: くろまめいりちらしずし
name.en: Kuromame-iri Chirashi-zushi (Mixed Sushi with black bean)

summary.text: The Katsuei area (Mimasaka City, Katsuo Town, Nagi Town, and Nishiawakura Village), located in the northeastern part of Okayama Prefecture, is one of the leading black bean production areas in Japan. The black beans produced in the Katsuei area are named Sakushu Guro and are branded as such. These large, tasty black beans are attractive, and various products such as tea and edamame made from Sakushu Guro are being developed and marketed throughout the country.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

summary.text: A hot pot dish where soba flour is shaped like loaches (Japanese freshwater fish). This dish is eaten in mountainous areas and is known for being easily digestible and warming the body. It features dashi (=Japanese soup stock) made with river fish.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

name.en: Tofu Meshi (Rice with Tofu and Vegetable Toppings)

summary.text: Tofu is an ingredient frequently used for Buddhist vegetarian cuisine. It was served by merchant families for Buddhist ceremonies. Tofu is inexpensive and easily available which is why it is used for a variety of local dishes. Raw tofu is mashed and then boiled. The water of the tofu is drained by squeezing the tofu with a cloth. It is then roasted, seasoned with soy sauce, and strained. The tofu is placed on top of a bowl of rice along with a variety of vegetables. This dish is eaten with soup.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

summary.text: "Mamakarizushi" is a type of "nigirizushi" (oval-shaped mounds of rice) made with "mamakari" (=Japanese scaled sardine) pickled in vinegar. A piece of pickled "mamakari" is placed on top of each mound of sushi rice. Another name for this ray-finned fish is "sappa". It is said that the fish became known as "mamakari" as people would often say, "mama wo kari ni iku hodo oishi", which means that the fish is so delicious that people would borrow rice to enjoy it.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

summary.text: Yuzu is a seasonal fruit which adds a pleasant aroma and flavor to dishes. They are harvested each year from around October and are in season in December. "Yuzu miso" is made with yuzu peel, yuzu juice, and miso. It is an all-purpose seasoning that is made throughout the country where yuzu is grown. Ibara city is one of the largest producers of yuzu in Okayama prefecture and the recipe for "yuzu miso" is handed down from generation to generation in this region.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

summary.text: In the mountainous northern part of Okayama Prefecture, a surprisingly large number of fish dishes have been handed down from generation to generation. Saba-zushi is an autumn festival feast mainly made in the northern central part of Okayama Prefecture. In the old days, when transportation was not convenient, it was difficult to obtain perishable raw fish in mountain villages far from the seashore, so people thought of using fish brought in from Tottori Prefecture in the San-in region to make a feast for the autumn festival.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

summary.text: Vinegared mamakari is widely known as a local dish of Okayama Prefecture. "Mamakari" is the name of a small fish called in the Okayama region, and "sappa" in the Kanto region. It is mainly caught in the Seto Inland Sea, and its season is around October, when it is at its most delicious with a lot of fat.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

summary.text: Hiruzen Okowa is a type of rice with many ingredients, generally called Gomoku Okowa. It is a local delicacy representative of Hiruzen, and always appears at festivals and celebrations. It is characterized by the sumptuous contents of chicken, chestnuts, burdocks, carrots, konnyaku, azuki beans, and seasonal wild vegetables from the Hiruzen area.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

summary.text: The first day of the sixth month of the lunar calendar, after rice planting was completed and the end of the rainy season was approaching, was a day when farmers everywhere took a break from work. This day also marks the border between the end of a bad year and the beginning of a new year, and various events are held on this day. During this period, farmers used to make "Kenbikiyaki," which is wrapped in myoga leaves and grilled.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

summary.text: “Todomese” is sushi simmered in a mixture of rice and vinegar. Its history stretches back to the Kamakura period of the Middle Ages. Back then, the “Fukuoka Market” was held in Bizen, Fukuoka (in modern day, Osafune Town in Fukuoka and Setouchi City in Okayama), which thrived as a commercial city with water transportation. As such, once drunken samurai added sour doburoku (unrefined sake) to the rice and meals cooked by the Takase River boatmen, it became more delicious.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

summary.text: Hinase is a town located in the southeastern part of Okayama prefecture, on the border of Hyogo prefecture. As sung in the ancient Hinase Kouta, many fish come to the Seto Inland Sea to spawn in the spring, thus animating the fishing grounds. As depicted in its kanji character, Spanish mackerel is particularly representative of a springtime fish. From the middle of the Meiji era, Sawara no Kōko Sushi started being made with Spanish mackerel to celebrate a bountiful catch and to pray for the safety of fishermen.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

summary.text: Kusagina are the dried young leaves of kusagi, a plant which grows wild in the countryside. It has an incredibly strong smell, so you'll know it's there even if you're just walking nearby. When you harvest it matters; select egg-sized ones that are neither too small nor too large. In the central region of Okayama Prefecture, it's picked and dried in late May. To dry it, quickly blanch the freshly picked leaves, then run it under cold water to remove the scum. It will not taste good unless all the scum is carefully removed.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）

summary.text: Yubeshi is a rice cake confection made with yuzu and walnuts, historically developed as a portable and preservable food but also given as a gift, with roots in many regions of the country. The Yubeshi made in the Tohoku and Kanto regions contain walnuts, but in Okayama prefecture, where large amounts of yuzu are produced, Yubeshi is made with yuzu. Takahashi City and Yakage Town are representative regions, with a history dating back to the Edo period.
summary.license: 出典：農林水產省（公共データ利用規約 第1.0版）
